content:
- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) in recent days, model tends to underestimate prices; increase forecast slightly.
- Model often overshoots after a spike in price (e.g., +1.5+ in 30d forecast), especially if sentiment was neutral or positive prior; cap forecast at 10–15% below true peak.
- Model underestimates mean-reverting periods (e.g., after 70–72 range), especially if sentiment is mixed or negative; add 2–5% to forecast to capture rebound.
- For 30d horizon, model consistently underestimates true price by 0.5–1.5% in early cycles (e.g., 2025-07-21/22), suggesting a lag in reaction to sentiment shifts; adjust downward by 0.3–0.7% for first 5–7 days.
- If sentiment history shows a sharp reversal (e.g., -1.0 to +1.0 in 3–5 days), model often fails to adjust forecast; apply a 1–2% correction in direction of sentiment shift.
